title: Identifying and Sorting Antigen-Specific B Cells from Plasmodium-Infected Mice
author: Calôba, Minns, et al.
materials: MojoSort mouse pan B cell isolation kit II

steps.title: Euthanize mice
steps.instruction: Sacrifice mice using CO₂ inhalation in a chamber until they become unconscious and cease moving, then confirm death by performing cervical dislocation.

steps.title: Harvest spleens into RP‑1
steps.instruction: Collect each spleen into a tube containing 3 mL RP‑1 buffer and keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Process spleens through a 180 µm wire‑mesh screen placed in a 10 cm petri dish, washing repeatedly with RP‑1 to obtain a high‑yield cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Transfer spleen and 3 mL RP‑1 to the petri dish with the mesh.
Using a syringe piston, press the spleen through the mesh.
Force 4 mL fresh RP‑1 through the mesh with a pipette gun set to high speed.
Aspirate the entire volume (≈7 mL) and wash the mesh again.
Transfer the collected cells to a 15 mL tube.
Repeat the force‑wash‑aspirate cycle at least three times to maximize yield.

steps.title: Lyse red blood cells
steps.instruction: Perform ACK lysis on the splenocyte suspension, neutralize, filter, and keep cells on ice.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant, vortex or slide tubes to dislodge the pellet.
Add 1 mL ACK lysis buffer, mix with a P1000 pipette.
Add an additional 2 mL ACK lysis buffer (total 3 mL for small spleens, 4 mL for large spleens).
Incubate 2–3 min at 25 °C (do not exceed this time).
Add fresh RP‑1 to bring the volume to 14 mL to neutralize the lysis buffer.
Centrifuge again at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL RP‑1 and filter through a 70‑µm mesh into a new 15 mL tube; keep on ice.
Take a 10 µL aliquot and count the cells.

steps.title: Count cells
steps.instruction: Take a 10 µL aliquot of the filtered suspension and determine cell concentration.

steps.title: Enrich B cells (negative selection)
steps.instruction: Use the MojoSort Pan B cell isolation kit to negatively select B cells, then wash and resuspend in PBS.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the single‑cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in RP‑1 to 1 × 10⁸ cells/mL.
Add 100 µL antibody mix per mL of cell suspension; mix with a P1000 pipette.
Incubate 15 min on ice.
Add 100 µL nanobeads per mL; mix gently.
Incubate 15 min on ice.
Add RP‑1 to a final volume of 2.5 mL, mix, and place the tube in the MojoSort magnet for 5 min.
Without removing the tube, hold the magnet and swiftly pour the liquid (enriched fraction) into a new 15 mL tube; keep this tube on ice.
Remove the tube from the magnet, add an additional 2.5 mL fresh RP‑1, resuspend the beads, and return the tube to the magnet for 5 min.
Again, without removing the tube, pour the liquid into the 15 mL tube that already contains the first enriched fraction (total 5 mL) and discard the beads.
Take an aliquot of the combined enriched cells for an unstained reference control.
Take a 10 µL aliquot and count the cells.
Add ice‑cold PBS to the combined enriched fraction to a final volume of 15 mL.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in 15 mL PBS, repeat the PBS wash once more, and keep the final suspension on ice.

steps.title: Live/Dead staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with Zombie Aqua viability dye diluted 1:1000 in PBS, incubate, then quench with RP‑1.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 1 mL diluted Live/Dead dye (1 µg/mL; 1:1000 dilution in PBS).
Incubate 20 min at 25 °C in the dark.
Add RP‑1 media to bring the total volume to 15 mL to neutralize the stain.

steps.title: SpyCage primary staining
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with FcBlock, decoy GreenCage, RedCage, and biotinylated anti‑scaffold antibody before magnetic enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL RP‑1.
Add 2 µg FcBlock (CD16/32) and 1.25 µg GreenCage‑PyUIS4 decoy; vortex gently 5 times.
Incubate 10 min at 25 °C in the dark.
Add 1.25 µg RedCage‑PyMSP1‑19; vortex gently.
Incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Add RP‑1 to a final volume of 15 mL.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 2 mL RP‑1.
Add 1 µg biotinylated anti‑scaffold antibody; vortex gently.
Incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Add RP‑1 to a final volume of 15 mL.

steps.title: SpyCage magnetic enrichment
steps.instruction: Capture SpyCage‑bound B cells with streptavidin nanobeads, separate labeled cells, and combine fractions.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells to 1 × 10⁸ cells/mL in RP‑1.
Add 100 µL MojoSort streptavidin nanobeads per mL; mix gently.
Incubate 15 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Add RP‑1 to a final volume of 15 mL.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 2.5 mL RP‑1.
Place the tube in the MojoSort magnet for 5 min.
Without removing the tube, hold the magnet and swiftly pour the unlabeled (flow‑through) fraction into a new FACS tube.
Remove the tube from the magnet and add 1 mL RP‑1 to keep the retained cells moist; this is “labeled fraction 1”.
Return the tube containing the unlabeled cells to the magnet for another 5 min.
Again, without removing the tube, pour and discard the remaining unlabeled fraction.
Remove the tube from the magnet, add 1 mL RP‑1, and combine this volume with “labeled fraction 1” to a final volume of 2 mL (final enriched SpyCage⁺ cell suspension).

description: B cells play a critical role in protection against malaria by secreting antibodies specific to a wide range of Plasmodium antigens.2,3,4,5,6,7,8 The protocol below describes the specific steps for infection of mice with Plasmodium yoelii-17XNL Clone 1.1 (Py), spleen harvest, preparation of splenic single cell suspension, staining of MSP1-19-specific B cells, as well as sorting live cells. Stained cells can be either used for phenotypic characterization using flow cytometry or for transcriptomic and epigenetic analysis using single-cell sequencing techniques. While we used this methodology to characterize memory B cells from Plasmodium-infected mice, this approach can be broadly applied to identify non-Plasmodium antigens in mice, when the right combination of “SpyCage” reagents is used.1.Prepare required buffers as described below.2.If needed, perform a trial run of the experiment to ascertain the minimum quantity of antibodies and enrichment kits necessary, as the size of the spleen and, therefore, the number of cells will vary depending on the time point of harvest post infection.
